reasoning: Recent Maine Senate polling is mixed but consistently close: a University of New Hampshire poll from July 15-20 showed Troy Jackson ahead of Susan Collins 49%-46%, while a Hart Research poll for Senate Majority PAC from July 27-August 1 showed Collins trailing 45%-49%. The best current read from these last-45-day sources is that the race is a narrow Democratic lean or near tie, roughly D+1 to D+3, with a practical snapshot around Jackson +3 based on the aggregate polling average cited in the latest polling summaries.

sources.name: University of New Hampshire Survey Center
sources.details: UNH Survey Center found Troy Jackson leading Susan Collins 49% to 46% among likely general-election voters, a 3-point Democratic margin.

sources.name: Portland Press Herald
sources.details: Press Herald reported the UNH poll showing Jackson at 49% and Collins at 46% in the Maine Senate matchup.

sources.name: Hart Research / Senate Majority PAC
sources.details: Hart Research polling for Senate Majority PAC found Jackson ahead of Collins 49% to 45%, a 4-point Democratic margin.

sources.name: WGME
sources.details: WGME reported Hart Research's poll showing Jackson leading Collins 49% to 45% in the Maine Senate race.

sources.name: PollsMax polling average
sources.details: PollsMax’s aggregate for the Maine Senate race shows a polling average of 45.4% Jackson to 48.5% Collins, corresponding to a Republican lead of 3.1 points.

sources.name: FiftyPlusOne polling average
sources.details: FiftyPlusOne’s Maine Senate polling average shows Jackson at 48.5% and Collins at 45.6%, a 2.9-point Democratic lead.
